articles.title: Navanethem 'Navi' Pillay Wins 2026 Nobel Peace Prize
articles.excerpt: The 85-year-old South African jurist of Indian Tamil descent was honoured by the Norwegian Nobel Committee for her efforts to promote peace and international law, from anti-apartheid activism to landmark war-crimes rulings.
articles.image_caption: Navanethem 'Navi' Pillay smiles during a public address. The Norwegian Nobel Committee awarded the 85-year-old South African jurist the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize for her efforts to promote peace and international law.
articles.nri_angle: Indian-origin South African jurist Navi Pillay's Nobel Peace Prize is a landmark diaspora recognition — a descendant of Tamil indentured labourers honoured for shaping global justice.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Entry-Level Jobs Shrink 25% as AI Reshapes Hiring for Indian Freshers
articles.excerpt: Automation is pulling away the bottom rung of the career ladder: entry-level IT hiring is down as much as a quarter, GCCs are cutting thousands of roles, and 70% of young Indians say landing a first job is harder than it was three years ago.
articles.image_caption: A close-up of a newspaper jobs classifieds headline. Entry-level hiring in Indian IT has fallen by as much as 25% as automation takes over routine tasks freshers once did.
articles.nri_angle: Indian students and fresh graduates, both in India and abroad (notably the 1.44 lakh Indians on US OPT facing a proposed $70,000 work-authorization fee), are hit by automation cutting entry-level hiring just as they enter the workforce.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: At Three, This Indian-American Boy Became the World's Youngest Male Author
articles.excerpt: Advay Jain of South Brunswick, New Jersey, wrote 'Dino Learns Not To Waste Food' at age three — earning a Guinness World Record and a felicitation from India's Consul General in New York.
articles.image_caption: Children's picture books. Four-year-old Advay Jain of New Jersey entered Guinness World Records as the youngest male to publish a book, at 3 years and 345 days old.
articles.nri_angle: An Indian-American preschooler setting a Guinness World Record is community pride — and a parenting story about encouraging, rather than correcting, a toddler's creativity.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: NRI Property Sales in India: TDS Rules Every Buyer Must Get Right
articles.excerpt: TDS on a property bought from an NRI is 12.5% of the full sale price — not 1% — and from October 1 the buyer's TAN requirement is gone. Here is the compliance checklist.
articles.image_caption: Residential apartment buildings in Malabar Hills, Mumbai. NRIs selling property in India face strict TDS rules buyers must get right.
articles.nri_angle: This is the definitive compliance guide for NRIs selling Indian property and the resident buyers who must deduct the correct TDS — a 12.5% vs 1% trap that routinely costs buyers penalties.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: From India U19 to Team USA: Saurabh Netravalkar's Unlikely Cricket Journey
articles.excerpt: A Mumbai boy who gave up professional cricket for a Cornell engineering degree rebuilt his career on weekend club games in California — and became the face of America's rise at the 2024 T20 World Cup.
articles.image_caption: Saurabh Netravalkar celebrates in the USA jersey during the 2024 T20 World Cup. The left-arm pacer’s Super Over heroics against Pakistan made him one of the faces of American cricket’s rise.
articles.nri_angle: Netravalkar's journey — from Mumbai's age-group cricket to a Cornell engineering degree and an Oracle career in California to starring for Team USA — captures the Indian-American experience of carrying two identities, and he has become one of the faces of cricket's growth in the United States.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Sharjah Wants $3 Billion From Indian Investors as Hormuz Chaos Reshapes Trade
articles.excerpt: Invest in Sharjah CEO Mohamed Juma Al Musharrkh says the emirate is targeting $3 billion in Indian investment by 2027, with a $2 billion Khorfakkan port upgrade and Hormuz disruptions pulling cargo to the UAE's east coast.
articles.image_caption: A container ship berths at a Gulf port terminal under gantry cranes. Sharjah is pitching its ports — led by a $2 billion Khorfakkan upgrade — as Hormuz disruptions reroute cargo to the UAE's east coast.
articles.nri_angle: The UAE's 3.3 million Indians form the world's largest NRI community, and Sharjah's industrial base already runs on Indian talent and capital — the $3 billion pitch creates direct investment and job opportunities for NRI entrepreneurs and professionals.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: USPS Unveils New Rangoli Diwali Stamp Ahead of Festival Ceremony
articles.excerpt: The Forever stamp, featuring artist Sangita Bhutada's rangoli photographed by Bijay Dixit, will be unveiled Oct. 21 at the Embassy of India in Washington — a decade after the first U.S. Diwali stamp.
articles.image_caption: A rangoli of lit diyas in Goa. The USPS unveiled its new Rangoli Diwali stamp ahead of the festival ceremony.
articles.nri_angle: A Diwali stamp is among the most visible forms of mainstream U.S. recognition for Indian Americans, placing Hindu festival imagery on everyday mail a decade after the community's 2016 campaign win.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Thousands of Minnesotans May Be Canadian Citizens Without Knowing It
articles.excerpt: A change to Canada's Citizenship Act that took effect in December 2025 removed the first-generation limit — and with it, the cap on how far back claims can run.
articles.image_caption: The Minneapolis skyline seen from the Stone Arch Bridge. More than 47,000 Minnesotans report Canadian or French Canadian ancestry, and a December 2025 law change may make many of them dual Canadian-American citizens.
articles.nri_angle: The C-3 change directly affects Indian-Canadian families who moved to the US: US-born children of Canadian citizens, once cut off by the first-generation limit, may now already be Canadian citizens.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Chennai's 'Wall of Hope' Gives Young Voices a Canvas on Mental Health
articles.excerpt: The youth-led installation, unveiled at the IIT Madras Research Park by SCARF's Department of Youth Mental Health, opens days ahead of World Mental Health Day.
articles.image_caption: Velachery Balu via flickr (BY-SA)
articles.nri_angle: The youth-led mental health wall at IIT Madras Research Park reflects a stigma-fighting model that matters to NRI families worried about pressures on young people both in India and abroad.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Nick Grewal Named 2026 Entrepreneur of the Year for Building ePropelled
articles.excerpt: The New Hampshire Tech Alliance honored the ePropelled founder at its October 6 Innovation Summit, capping a four-decade career that runs from Nashoba Networks to a global propulsion company with an engineering center in Chennai.
articles.image_caption: ePropelled founder and CEO Nick Grewal (left) poses with former New Hampshire Governor Chris Sununu. Grewal was named the New Hampshire Tech Alliance's 2026 Entrepreneur of the Year at its October 6 Innovation Summit in Nashua.
articles.nri_angle: ePropelled's engineering and development center in Chennai puts Indian engineers at the heart of a global propulsion-tech supply chain, linking Grewal's recognition directly to Indian tech talent.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Brooklyn Comic Pooja Reddy Turns Kentucky Roots Into Country Cabaret
articles.excerpt: Her one-woman show "Pooja Reddy is White Trash" at Joe's Pub uses stand-up and original country songs to explore a South Indian upbringing in rural Kentucky.
articles.image_caption: The Public Theater on Lafayette Street in Manhattan, whose Joe's Pub venue hosted the premiere of Brooklyn comic Pooja Reddy's one-woman country cabaret, 'Pooja Reddy is White Trash,' this September.
articles.nri_angle: A second-generation Indian American turning a small-town Southern upbringing into art — Reddy's show speaks directly to diaspora kids raised far from any desi enclave, who grew up as the only brown face in the room.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Krishnamoorthi Condemns 240% Surge in Anti-South Asian Hate Posts on X
articles.excerpt: The Illinois Democrat cited a new study counting 542,360 hateful posts targeting South Asians in 18 months, and named a Texas candidate's post and a DHS graphic as examples.
articles.image_caption: Rep. Raja Krishnamoorthi (D-Ill.), who condemned the surge in anti-South Asian hate posts on X.
articles.nri_angle: Directly about the South Asian American experience: a measurable 240% surge in online hate, tied by a leading Indian American lawmaker to mainstream political rhetoric — a civil-rights issue the community is being asked to confront publicly.
tags: Center for the Study of Organized Hate
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Ghana to Seek BRICS Membership, Asks India's Backing During Jaishankar Visit
articles.excerpt: Ghana's cabinet has decided to pursue BRICS membership and asked New Delhi to guide its bid; the two sides also signed MoUs on agriculture and science and technology during the EAM's October 6–7 visit.
articles.image_caption: External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar with Ghana's President John Mahama in Accra. Ghana is seeking India's backing for BRICS membership. (PTI)
articles.nri_angle: Ghana hosts one of West Africa's most established Indian business communities in trade, manufacturing, and pharmaceuticals — the exact sectors both governments prioritized, and a BRICS seat with Indian backing could ease the path for Indian firms operating there.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Flydubai Co-Pilot Confesses Gaza Revenge Motive, Had Planned Ben Gurion Crash
articles.excerpt: Hamam al-Hammami told investigators he sought an airline job to carry out the attack and wanted to die a martyr; investigators are now probing whether he acted alone, while Captain Smit Machchhar recovers from a fractured skull.
articles.image_caption: A Flydubai Boeing 737-800. Co-pilot Hamam al-Hammami allegedly planned to crash Flight FZ1073 into Ben Gurion Airport in revenge for Gaza.
articles.nri_angle: An Indian pilot's heroism saved Flight FZ1073, and his recovery continues; the case also spotlights aviation-security gaps that matter to the millions of Indians who fly Gulf routes every year.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Young Astronomers Shine With Four Golds and a Silver in Hanoi
articles.excerpt: All five Indian students medalled at the 19th International Olympiad on Astronomy and Astrophysics, placing India joint third among 64 countries in the biggest IOAA ever held.
articles.image_caption: The Indian team holds the national flag at the 19th International Olympiad on Astronomy and Astrophysics in Hanoi, medals around their necks. All five students medalled — four golds and one silver — placing India joint third among 64 countries.
articles.nri_angle: The IOAA triumph gives diaspora families a concrete window into India's HBCSE Olympiad pipeline — the training system behind the medals and a path many Indian-origin students abroad try to emulate — while underscoring the strength of the science education system many diaspora careers were built on.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Chennai's Indian Fine Arts Society Honours Its Young Carnatic Stars
articles.excerpt: More than 20 children took prizes at the 93-year-old sabha's annual music competition, with top winners receiving Thanjavur tamburas at a ceremony in Alwarpet on Sunday.
articles.image_caption: Winners of the Indian Fine Arts Society's annual music competition pose with their prizes in Chennai. More than 20 children received prizes at the ceremony on Sunday.
articles.nri_angle: NRIs planning Margazhi-season trips to Chennai can catch this next generation of Carnatic musicians as they move from student competitions onto the December concert stage.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Rahul Gandhi Accuses Delhi Police of Silencing Women Over Harassment Complaints
articles.excerpt: The Leader of Opposition said women protesters and journalists faced mistreatment by Delhi Police during October 3 demonstrations at Jantar Mantar, and demanded CCTV footage from Saket police station be made public.
articles.image_caption: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi. Gandhi accused Delhi Police of silencing women over harassment complaints after meeting two journalists who alleged assault at Saket police station.
articles.nri_angle: Overseas Indians follow Indian political developments closely; the standoff adds another flashpoint to the SIR controversy and the broader debate over policing of protests and press freedom in the world's largest democracy.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Rahul Vohra: The ₹144 Crore LinkedIn Exit That Taught Him Balance
articles.excerpt: The British-Indian Superhuman co-founder sold Rapportive to LinkedIn for a reported $15 million months after collapsing from exhaustion. The health crisis rewired how he builds companies — and he has meditated twice daily ever since.
articles.image_caption: Rahul Vohra, founder of Superhuman and Rapportive. (yespress.io)
articles.nri_angle: Vohra's Birmingham-to-Silicon-Valley arc, and his public break with the diaspora's outwork-everyone script, give Indian-origin professionals in high-pressure roles a concrete founder-tested case for designing stamina instead of burning through it.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: San Jose Seventh-Grader Boosts Air-to-Water Output 117%, Reaches National STEM Final
articles.excerpt: Ankith Burki built an atmospheric water generator from scratch, found that low-frequency sound waves dramatically increased its water collection, and earned a finalist spot in the 2026 Thermo Fisher Scientific Junior Innovators Challenge.
articles.image_caption: San Jose seventh-grader Ankith Burki. His air-to-water prototype reached the national final of the 2026 Thermo Fisher Scientific Junior Innovators Challenge.
articles.nri_angle: For Indian-American families, Burki's achievement shows diaspora youth using STEM to tackle water scarcity — a problem with deep relevance to India, where water stress affects hundreds of millions.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: GIFT City Emerges as NRI Magnet With $54 Billion Banking Push
articles.excerpt: Nearly 500 wealthy Indians used the FCNR(B) facility through the GIFT IFSC for the first time — many discovering the financial centre for the first time — and regulators are moving to keep them with bigger investments.
articles.image_caption: K Rajaraman, chairman of the International Financial Services Centres Authority (IFSCA), the unified regulator of GIFT City. Rajaraman said nearly 500 high-net-worth NRIs used the FCNR(B) facility through the GIFT IFSC for the first time.
articles.nri_angle: GIFT City is built for how NRIs handle money: dollar-denominated investing with no INR conversion, no transaction taxes and unrestricted repatriation through a single Indian-regulated financial centre.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indian American Geneticist Pradeep Natarajan to Receive AHA's 2026 Population Research Prize
articles.excerpt: The Harvard and Mass General physician-scientist, who joined Amgen in August to lead human genetics, will be honored on Nov. 8 in Chicago for transforming how genetics and big population studies prevent heart disease.
articles.image_caption: Dr. Pradeep Natarajan, the Harvard Medical School and Massachusetts General Hospital cardiovascular geneticist. He will receive the American Heart Association’s 2026 Population Research Prize on Nov. 8 in Chicago.
articles.nri_angle: Dr. Pradeep Natarajan's AHA prize is a milestone for Indian Americans in medical research — and his polygenic heart-risk work speaks directly to South Asians, who face among the highest cardiovascular risk of any group.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Two Teenagers Jailed 10 Years for Petrol Arson Attack on Indian Restaurant in London
articles.excerpt: The Old Bailey heard the August 2025 attack on Indian Aroma in Gants Hill was a 'sophisticated and professional operation' that left a couple in their 20s with life-changing burns.
articles.image_caption: Image: @narindertweets via X
articles.nri_angle: Indian restaurants are community anchors across the UK; an attack of this severity on a family-run eatery resonates with the million-plus Indian diaspora in Britain and its business owners.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Telangana Woman Killed in Missouri Truck Crash; Family Seeks Help to Bring Body Home
articles.excerpt: Daram Supriya, 31, from Mahabubabad district, died after a speeding truck hit her car in Missouri; the family has appealed for help bringing her body home for final rites.
articles.image_caption: Daram Supriya, 31, from Maripeda in Telangana's Mahabubabad district, in a photo published by IndiaToday with its report on the crash. She died after the car she was traveling in was struck from behind by a speeding truck in Missouri on October 4, 2026.
articles.nri_angle: A Telugu worker's death in Missouri leaves her Mahabubabad family navigating the painful, slow process of repatriating her body — a recurring ordeal for the Indian diaspora.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Bangladesh Presses India to Speed Up Sheikh Hasina Extradition
articles.excerpt: Indian High Commissioner Dinesh Trivedi said New Delhi cannot commit to a timeline, stressing that the extradition request is being examined through an established legal process under the bilateral treaty.
articles.image_caption: Sheikh Hasina, Bangladeshs former prime minister, speaks at an event with the Bangladeshi flag behind her. Dhaka has asked India to expedite her extradition so she can face charges at home.
articles.nri_angle: The extradition standoff shapes India-Bangladesh relations, which touch the millions of people with family, business, and cultural ties across the border, as well as the flow of trade and travel between the two countries.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: UK's Oldest Indian Restaurant Accuses Crown Estate of Cultural Ignorance in Eviction Row
articles.excerpt: Veeraswamy, serving diners on London's Regent Street since 1926, is fighting the Crown Estate's refusal to renew its lease — a dispute whose court hearing has now been delayed until at least late autumn.
articles.image_caption: A doorman in Veeraswamy uniform stands outside the restaurant’s facade at Victory House on Regent Street. The century-old restaurant is fighting the Crown Estate’s refusal to renew its lease, a dispute whose court hearing has been delayed until at least late autumn 2026.
articles.nri_angle: A century-old Indian institution on London's Regent Street is fighting to survive against its royal landlord, making the case that Indian heritage in Britain deserves protection from commercial redevelopment.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Ranveer Singh Becomes Ray-Ban's First Brand Ambassador in India
articles.excerpt: The Bollywood star will front Ray-Ban and Ray-Ban Meta in India, headlining the 'Frame Your True Self' campaign as Meta's Gen 3 smart glasses go on sale starting at ₹44,300.
articles.image_caption: Ranveer Singh wears round Ray-Ban sunglasses and a red leather jacket in a campaign portrait. Ray-Ban named him its first brand ambassador in India on October 1, 2026.
articles.nri_angle: An Indian film star fronting a global brand's AI-eyewear push in India gives the diaspora a cultural foothold in a technology launch that will shape how wearables are received across South Asia.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India-Born Scientist Shankar Balasubramanian Wins 2026 Wolf Chemistry Prize
articles.excerpt: The Cambridge chemist shares the award with David Klenerman and Pascal Mayer for the DNA-sequencing technology that cut the cost of reading a human genome from over $1 billion to about $1,000.
articles.image_caption: Shankar Balasubramanian, a chemistry professor at the University of Cambridge, in a university portrait. He shared the 2026 Wolf Prize in Chemistry for the DNA-sequencing technology behind Solexa/Illumina.
articles.image_credit: Nathan Pitt / University of Cambridge via hayadan.com
articles.nri_angle: An India-born chemist winning the Wolf Prize — one year after an Indian American physicist won it — marks a second straight year of Indian-diaspora laureates at one of science's top honors.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indian American Leaders Press MEA Secretary on Passports, Property Fraud in New York
articles.excerpt: In the first meeting of its kind, Secretary (CPV & OIA) Sripriya Ranganathan's US outreach tour reached New York, where diaspora leaders raised passport renewal hassles, VFS service gaps and grabbed NRI land back home.
articles.image_caption: Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri, who was pressed by Indian American leaders on passports and property fraud issues
articles.nri_angle: For the first time, MEA's diaspora chief is doing a multi-city US listening tour — New York Indian-Americans used the opening to put bread-and-butter grievances like passport hassles and grabbed NRI land on the record ahead of Pravasi Bharatiya Divas.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Dubai Crown Prince Visits Injured Indian Pilot Smit Machchhar in Hospital
articles.excerpt: Sheikh Hamdan praised flydubai captain Smit Machchhar for 'the highest degrees of courage' after the FZ1073 cockpit attack, as UAE prosecutors said the co-pilot had attempted a terrorist act.
articles.image_caption: Dubai Crown Prince Sheikh Hamdan bin Mohammed holds the hand of flydubai captain Smit Machchhar during a hospital visit on October 3, 2026. The Crown Prince praised Machchhar for embodying the highest degrees of courage after the September 30 cockpit attack on flight FZ1073.
articles.nri_angle: Dubai's top leadership publicly adopting an Indian pilot as 'part of the story of our nation' signals how much the Gulf's 4-million-strong Indian diaspora matters to the Emirates.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Delhi Speaker Vijender Gupta Meets Indian Diaspora in Lima, Pushes Business and Cultural Ties
articles.excerpt: During his Peru visit, Gupta praised the diaspora as ambassadors of Indian culture and held talks on expanding Indian business presence in Peru and neighbouring markets.
articles.image_caption: Delhi Assembly Speaker Vijender Gupta, who met members of the Indian diaspora in Lima, Peru.
articles.nri_angle: For the small but growing Indian community in Peru — far from the spotlight of US or Gulf diaspora events — a visit from an Indian legislature's presiding officer is a rare recognition that their bridge role matters to New Delhi.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Netanyahu Calls Indian Flydubai Captain Smit Machchhar a 'True Hero', Invites Him to Israel
articles.excerpt: In a personal call on October 3, Israel's prime minister invited the hospitalised pilot — and Narendra Modi — to light a flame at Israel's Independence Day ceremony next May.
articles.image_caption: Sand artist Sudarsan Pattnaik created this tribute to flydubai Captain Smit Machchhar in Puri. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu called Machchhar a "true hero" and invited him to Israel on October 3.
articles.nri_angle: An Indian pilot saved by instinct is now a symbol of India-Israel partnership — with Netanyahu drawing Prime Minister Modi himself into next May's Independence Day ceremony.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: From 23-Year-Old Trailblazer to State Senate: Indian American Nabeela Syed Launches Illinois Bid
articles.excerpt: Syed, who flipped a Republican-held Illinois House seat in 2022 as the first South Asian elected to the state legislature, is running for the 26th Senate District on a healthcare and affordability platform.
articles.image_caption: Nabeela Syed sits on the steps of Doe Memorial Library at the University of California, Berkeley. The Indian American state representative, first elected to the Illinois House at 23, has launched her campaign for the Illinois State Senate 26th District.
articles.nri_angle: Syed is a first-generation Indian American Muslim whose grassroots rise offers a model for young South Asian political engagement in the US.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Georgia's Sirish Subash Wins Top Young Scientist Title for AI Pesticide Detector
articles.excerpt: The 14-year-old Indian-origin ninth grader's handheld device PestiSCAND detects pesticide residues on produce with over 85% accuracy, earning him the 2024 3M Young Scientist Challenge's $25,000 grand prize.
articles.nri_angle: The win extends a strong run of Indian-origin students dominating American STEM competitions, mentored and rooted in a diaspora family's values.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Skyroot's Pawan Chandana Named to TIME100 Next 2026 After Vikram-1 Orbital Triumph
articles.excerpt: The Skyroot Aerospace co-founder and CEO joins TIME's annual list of 100 emerging global leaders, months after his company's Vikram-1 became the first Indian private rocket to reach orbit.
articles.image_caption: Skyroot Aerospace's Vikram-S rocket ahead of its Mission Prarambh suborbital flight in November 2022, which paved the way for the Vikram-1 orbital triumph
articles.nri_angle: Pawan Chandana's TIME100 Next listing spotlights India's private space sector — built by engineers who stayed in India — as a new destination for diaspora aerospace talent and global investment.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Bodhana Sivanandan, 11, Earns Third Guinness Title as Youngest Woman Grandmaster
articles.excerpt: Guinness World Records has officially recognised the Indian-origin British prodigy as the youngest chess player ever to earn the Woman Grandmaster title, following her performance at the 2026 Chess Olympiad in Samarkand.
articles.nri_angle: Indian-origin British schoolgirl Bodhana Sivanandan, daughter of Tamil Nadu parents, earns her third Guinness World Records title — a point of pride for the British-Indian community and diaspora worldwide.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Bricks Hurled at Ohio Hindu Temple During Prayers, Windows Shattered
articles.excerpt: The Shree Swaminarayan Vadtal Dham Hindu Mandir in Richmond Heights was struck around 1:30 pm on Friday while priests and devotees were inside. No arrests have been reported, and surveillance footage is under review.
articles.image_caption: Shattered glass lies scattered across the floor inside the Shree Swaminarayan Vadtal Dham Hindu Mandir after the attack. The Richmond Heights, Ohio temple was struck with bricks on Friday afternoon while priests and devotees were inside.
articles.nri_angle: The attack targeted a place of worship for Hindu Americans in Ohio during prayers, sharpening community fears about temple safety and the response to anti-Hindu hate in the US.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: RCMP Arrests Five in Extortion Probe Targeting British Columbia Car Dealership
articles.excerpt: The coordinated arrests followed a year-long RCMP investigation, Project E_PURSUANCE, into extortion demands, arson and shootings targeting an auto dealership's co-owners in Surrey and Langley.
articles.image_caption: An RCMP officer; the force arrested five in an extortion probe targeting British Columbia car dealerships.
articles.nri_angle: The arrests mark the first major break in a year-long wave of extortion targeting British Columbia's South Asian community, whose members police are now urging to cooperate as the investigation widens across Western Canada.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Faruk Patel Built a Rs 10,964 Crore Green Energy Empire From Rs 1 Lakh
articles.excerpt: The son of a bus conductor who once drove an auto and worked at Pizza Hut, Dr Faruk G. Patel built KP Group from a Rs 1 lakh trucking venture in 1994 into one of India's leading solar and wind conglomerates.
articles.image_caption: Faruk Patel, who built a Rs 10,964 crore green energy empire from Rs 1 lakh.
articles.nri_angle: UK-based writer Imtiaz Patel Varediwala's biography of Patel (in English, Gujarati and audiobook) gives diaspora readers a documented playbook of a first-generation Indian entrepreneur — and a model for investing back home.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Shabana Azmi, Naseeruddin Shah Join Mumbai Protest Demanding Election Chief's Ouster
articles.excerpt: Thousands gathered at Shivaji Park for the Cockroach Janta Party's demonstration seeking the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged electoral-roll irregularities.
articles.image_caption: Protesters gather at Shivaji Park in Mumbai during the Cockroach Janta Party demonstration on October 2. Veteran actors Naseeruddin Shah and Shabana Azmi and singer Vishal Dadlani joined the protest demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.
articles.nri_angle: The protest over electoral-roll integrity resonates with NRIs who closely follow the health of Indian democracy and have family members voting back home.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Newsom Appoints Indian American Ajay Bhutoria to California Engineering Board
articles.excerpt: The Fremont tech leader and former Biden AANHPI commission member will serve as a public member of the California Board for Professional Engineers, Land Surveyors and Geologists.
articles.image_caption: Ajay Bhutoria, Indian American technology executive and civic leader from Fremont, California. Governor Gavin Newsom appointed Bhutoria as a public member of the California Board for Professional Engineers, Land Surveyors and Geologists.
articles.nri_angle: Bhutoria's appointment puts a prominent Indian American immigration advocate — a champion of green-card backlog relief and H-1B reform — in a California regulatory leadership role.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: 'Go Home' Row Escalates: Krishnamoorthi Doubles Down as Dhillon Reveals Daily Racist Attacks
articles.excerpt: What began as a Florida councilman's 'take your curry and go home' jibe has widened into a bipartisan reckoning, with Trump's civil rights chief disclosing identity attacks and new data showing half of Indian Americans report discrimination.
articles.image_caption: US Representative Raja Krishnamoorthi speaks at a podium.
articles.nri_angle: The episode has become a defining test of belonging for Indian Americans, the community repeatedly targeted in the Florida councilman's remarks.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Diwali Returns to London's National Maritime Museum With a New Bazaar
articles.excerpt: The free 'All Together Now' festival on 7 November adds a Diwali Bazaar of South Asian designers to a programme of performances, workshops and talks in Greenwich.
articles.image_caption: Dancers in red and white traditional dress perform at the National Maritime Museum's Diwali celebration as a large crowd looks on. This year's festival, All Together Now, runs on 7 November and adds a first-ever Diwali Bazaar to the free day-long programme.
articles.nri_angle: The festival is aimed squarely at Britain's Indian and South Asian communities, with programming — food talks, identity panels, sustainable fashion — that reflects how the diaspora keeps Diwali today.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk
